searchText: <@&1417820113981145228> I would appreciate reviews on the EIP-8282 consensus-specs PR. We want to merge this & create a release within the next ~10 hours. https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5359 I don't have the rights to unresolve comments I think what do you want unresolved? left a comment on the issue of using withdrawal credentials to be the builder version, which I think should be unresolved Meaning that it's 0x03 instead of 0x00? no, meaning that it allows for anything I unresolved it I understand but I'm not sure that I agree. The way I see it, we should only allow 0x00 or we should allow everything. I don't see a situation in which we ignore a deposit because of something in the withdrawal credentials, other than a bad signature. If someone wants to make a 0x01 builder right now, they just might not be able to participate if the withdrawal creds are interpreted differently, ie a new field in those 11 empty bytes after the version. They would need to exit & re-deposit. For example, it's entirely possible to make a 0x00 validator with an invalid pubkey right now. cc <@755590043632140352> But this reminds me, we should add a check in bid gossip validation that the builder's version is 0. And if we wanted, we could say that only 0x00 builders can exit. Three options, and pros and cons. 1) Leave as is: builders can create any version right now, so this makes it impossible for the protocol to later use versions to enforce behavior. This effectively makes versions kinda useless. 2) Enforce 0x00 for the first version at the fork. This is better than the above, it doesn't suffer from the above problem. 3) Do not enforce 0x00, but enforce a region. This is the best of both worlds: this doesn't suffer from the problem in 1 but at the same time it allows for offchain protocols to enforce whatever behavior they want on the version (eg a protocol that requires their proposers to only contact builders of version 0x07). I would say your assessment of 1 is false. We would just enforce it elsewhere, not at the builder structure. Give me a real example of this that is not just "execution address must be potuz.eth" you cannot enforce it elsewhere? I can send a request to the contract and create that version, how do you enforce it? What do you mean? We enforce things with 0x01 and 0x02 validators. Eg when consolidating, X must match Y. If this is a new builder structure field, we can just set all existing builders with that version to an invalid value. yes but we went with 2 for validators: you could not deposit a validator with withdrawal credentials 0x02 at genesis we didn't go with 1) No we didn't. You could always deposit a 0x02 validator. I'm pretty sure. To be clear, I'm talking about mainnet during phase0. can you explain me what the complain is here? why do you feel it's fine to allow any version to be created by builders? If you want a real example that is not send money to potuz.eth, here are a few possible future lines of exploration: 1) Builders of type 0xEF can also validate. 2) Builders of type 0xEF are required to send their payloads with a ZK proof 3) Builders of type 0xEF get issuance from the protocol, or pay issuance to the protocol.. is the problem that adding a single assert to not have a range is too complex? or can lose money to someone that uses non-standard tooling and creates a builder with the reserved domain? What is there to enforce here? Why should this be done when adding a builder to the registry? We can add those asserts in the functions when necessary? No? the enforcement is that there can't be a builder on the registry with a reserved version, so that when we actually want to use a version, for whatever reason, we are sure that before the fork where the version is allowed, there are no builders with that version. This allows us to use any kind of enforcement of the version, that would be impossible to enforce if builders existed before. Eg: in the future fork where we allow builders to also be post-quantum aggregators, they need to be staked at least 2K ETH, we would need to special case those preexisting builders that frontrun the fork, instead of simply not allowing them before the fork In this example, we'd just have a check somewhere that builder.balance is 2048. This wouldn't be enforced at deposit time. Eg in `process_pq_aggregate` we'd have checks like `assert builder.version == X` and `assert builder.balance >= 2048`. Does that make sense? These things can/should be enforced elsewhere. not necessarily: the logic can assume that the builder always has above 2K in the exact same way that we assume now that the builder has more than 1 **because** we enforced it at deposit time and it's impossible to go below. The whole point is that a single one line with a single assert enables **any** behavior we want in the future, while not having this reservation precludes us from using any behavior we want. So again, I have given you a few arguments why to add it, can you give me a single one why not to add it? notice that I don't mind enfocing 0x00, what I think it´s wrong is just allowing anything Can enforce at registry time doesn't mean we *must* enforce there. The three examples you gave above are not convincing lol. Reasons to allow any version: (1) This functions the same as validators do today. (2) If we introduce a new version of builder, we could have those ready at the fork; and not be in this awkward onboarding situation we currently face. (3) Limiting some versions would mean non-consecutive versions, ie a jump from version 0 to version 100. (4) These enforcements can be handled elsewhere. I'm not strongly opposed to reserving versions > 0x0F. Just in case we need to do whatever you describe. But also I just do not see us actually using that. But who knows. Maybe <@586161934425128960> can weigh in? Happy to do whatever at this point. Also, say there does exist a builder with version=0xEF and we need to impose some restrictions. We could just change the builder to version=0 at the fork or forcefully exit them, no? the reason why I left this comment was along the lines of what <@755590043632140352> is saying if you have to assert a 2nd conditions, what's the `version` actually useful for? just informational? but we do the same for validators right now so this might be fine It would be the same as 0x01 validators today. The withdrawal credentials can be interpreted differently. We do not enforce that the last 20 byte's of their withdrawal credential is a valid eth1 address. But we will happily interpret it as an address & send ETH to it. <@755590043632140352> <@586161934425128960> how about we just merge what we have and debate this more later. If core devs want to limit the version, we can do that. Not sure this is enough to delay the release & glamsterdam-devnet-6. When you have time, please open a PR with the `assert request.withdrawal_credentials[0] & 0xF0 == 0x00` change. I already approved it, leaving it up to <@755590043632140352> wouldn't this be a `continue` or `return`? Another PR to review. I hope this isn't controversial. Follow up from the 8282 PR which I said I would do. https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5377 😂 in the first PR I ask you to add an assert and you didn't like it... in this one I ask you to remove an assert, we'll see where we land 😅 Oh gosh lol. > then off protocol projects may want to use that If there's a will, there's a way. Nothing we do would prevent this. Also why should we care what people do off-protocol? And it's not about the assert. It's about what the assert does. yes, and I think the assert in the payload bid processing is also unnecessary 😢 why? Say we add a new builder version something else in the future, likely to happen. For something that wouldn't submit bids. Should they be allowed to submit bids? I'm just trying to think ahead a bit. I think it's a good idea to restrict that right now. funny that you think it's alright to restrict in every spot that uses a version, instead of on the single spot of creation of the builder, that would ensure that all other spots are satisfied. Yeah, because that would prevent onboarding of other versions before the fork. And it would burn deposits when accidentally depositing with a 0x03 credential. which is precisely why I am proposing that we simply reserve, in the single spot, some versions. Then you can add extra restrictions if you want on other spots Adding a restriction today, that is not used at all, and allowing them to exist, doesn't make much sense to me. But how would that solve the onboarding issue? Say 0x10 - 0xFF is reserved. If we introduce proof builders when mandatory proofs is included in an upgrade. Will it use 0x01 or 0x10? They can exist _before_ the fork & participate _after_ the fork. it depends on what we need to enforce: if the new type of builders **requires** that they could not have existed any builder before the fork, then we would use the reserved space, that's precisely the reason to have it. If the new type of builders does not have this requirement, then we can simply use the any index outside of the reserved space. The point of the reservation is to allow us to have more flexibility for unforeseen designs in the future. With the 0x10 - 0xFF reservation, we would still keep the version & checks defined in https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5377 ? And just have the reservation as a "just in case we need it" thing? The two things are independent, you can even have two reservation spaces. And 5377 would be equivalent to reserve != 0 for participation and nothing for existence. Reserving for participation is restrictive in that if we ever need to onboard a new type of builder that should exist before the next fork and could participate before the next fork, then asserting version == 0 precludes this from working. While if the assertion was version < 10, then we can onboard builders with version 9 for that role Anyway, this is getting out of hand over trivialities, I don't feel that strongly about 5377 as I do about the other one I was planning on merging this before making the release, but now I'm not sure if I can... it's ok to merge it's also OK not to add the assertions at all I feel more strongly about the other one being wrong to not reserve a space on the deposit processing, because that completely dissalows us from certain constructions, for no reason Alright thanks. I think I'm going to merge it and make the release. I think it's important to set the version to 0 when onboarding. I am open to reserving space for builder versions. Since starting this mini-debate, I have been convinced of its value and would probably support it as long as it doesn't prevent us from onboarding a new version before the fork. It is fine as long as we only enforce builder version on bid processing and gossip. So builder deposits via execution requests with non 0x0 version should be accepted. Also EL doesn't enforce builder version before passing the requests to us do they? That’s exactly how it works & no they don’t.

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content:
Three options, and pros and cons. 

1) Leave as is: builders can create any version right now, so this makes it impossible for the protocol to later use versions to enforce behavior. This effectively makes versions kinda useless.
2) Enforce 0x00 for the first version at the fork. This is better than the above, it doesn't suffer from the above problem.
3) Do not enforce 0x00, but enforce a region. This is the best of both worlds: this doesn't suffer from the problem in 1 but at the same time it allows for offchain protocols to enforce whatever behavior they want on the version (eg a protocol that requires their proposers to only contact builders of version 0x07).
